pinterest.title: Honeymoon Planner vs Travel Agent: The Questions That Show What You Will Get
pinterest.description: Honeymoon planner vs travel agent? The two titles overlap, because both are labels rather than job titles. Compare the service a particular business will actually provide. Ask everyone the same questions: who you will deal with from first call to return, what they will book and in whose name, how their fee is worked out, and what is confirmed in writing before you commit. Read the full guide.

pinterest.title: Questions to Ask Any Honeymoon Planner or Travel Agent Before You Book
pinterest.description: Put the same questions to any planner or agent and set the answers side by side. Whose terms apply to each booking? When are deposits due, and who holds them? Do you receive anything from suppliers, and is that disclosed? Will quotes be in Australian dollars? Who do we contact while we are travelling, and in which time zone? Ask for every answer in writing. Read the full guide.

pinterest.title: Planning a Honeymoon After a Destination Wedding: One Plan or Two?
pinterest.description: When the honeymoon begins where the wedding ends, the two trips share dates, flights and luggage. Ask any business you are considering whether it can plan the honeymoon together with your wedding travel, who checks that dates and flights line up if not, and whose name goes on the honeymoon tickets. Book travel in the name on your passport. Read the full guide.

slides: Honeymoon planner or travel agent? Both are labels, not job titles. Compare what each business will actually do.
Start with yourselves. How much of the planning do you want to hand over, and how many moving parts does the trip have?
Ask what they will do. Design the trip, or book what you choose? Who looks after flights, connections and the days in between?
Ask how they are paid. Is there a planning fee? Do they earn commission from the places they book, and is it shown to you?
Ask what happens when plans change. Whose terms apply to each booking, and who do you contact while you are away?
Your Australian consumer guarantees apply whether you book directly, through an agent or through a booking platform.
Honeymoon straight after a destination wedding? Ask whether the same business can plan both as one plan.

instagram_carousel.caption:
Honeymoon planner or travel agent? The two titles overlap, because both are labels rather than job titles. The useful comparison is the service a particular business will actually provide.

Put the same questions to anyone you are considering, ask for the answers in writing and set them side by side:
Who will we deal with from first call to return?
What will you book, and in whose name?
Whose terms apply to each booking?
How is your fee worked out, and is it agreed in writing before work begins?
Do you receive anything from suppliers, and is that disclosed?
Will quotes be in Australian dollars?
Who do we contact while we are travelling?

Australian consumer guarantees apply whichever label you choose. If you book through an intermediary, both its terms and the provider's apply, so ask to see both.

If the honeymoon follows a destination wedding, ask whether the same business can plan the wedding travel and the honeymoon as one plan.
